messages:
incident-bot: P1 page to +#oncall-sre +alex_oncall: Cerulean (enterprise, VPC) reporting elevated 5xxs for model inference endpoints in eu-west-1 dedicated pool. Incident ID: CER-2029-01. Trigger: 95th-percentile p99 errors > 30% and sustained CPU/GPU saturation. Please ack and investigate. :rotating_light:

alex_oncall: acked. I'm on it. @support-maya can you paste the customer error samples & any recent deploys?

support-maya: Cerulean reported ~11:03 UTC. They see repeated `HTTP 502` and `504` from our gateway when calling /v1/generate. No deploys from their side. No Redwood deploys in eu-west-1 since 08:45UTC. Customer estimate: ~40% of requests failing, some successful requests show latency spikes to 6-8s. Log snippets: ```{"req_id":"c-112233","err":"upstream reset by peer"}``` Also CIAM/tenant identity checks pass.

eng-ops-luis: looking at infra metrics: dedicated pool eu-west-1 for Cerulean is at 98-100% GPU utilization, host OOMs on two GPUs in the last 20m, KV cache eviction rate skyrocketed. Autoscaler tried to spin warm nodes but hit quota + scheduling delays. There are transient kernel retries on the runtime layer.

alex_oncall: possible mitigations: (1) fast traffic shift to Cerulean's warm standby in eu-west-2, (2) temporary per-tenant rate limit to protect pool, (3) DNS CNAME change + short TTL cutover. Thoughts?

sre_jamie: +1 to doing a weighted DNS shift into eu-west-2 staged 10/30/60/100. We should update Route53/managed DNS for cerulean.api.redwood-inference.com CNAME -> cerulean-eu-west-2-lb.redwood-inference.com, but TTL currently 300s so plan for step changes every 5m. Also we need to ensure the warm pool in eu-west-2 has pinned model version and KV primed.

netops-rita: confirm DNS owner. I can run the change but need an approved change file. Also we can advertise a temporary A record to cerulean-standby to bypass CNAME caching for their clients if they can honor host fallback. We should also add an IP allowlist for the standby load balancer if their VPC has strict peering.

customer-success-evan: Cerulean engineering can do client-side fallback if we tell them to switch an origin header or host. They are ready to accept a cutover but want staged traffic to avoid double-billing of inference units. We agreed to keep identical model & version so billing unaffected.

eng-ops-luis: KVs: I will trigger a KV warm sync to eu-west-2 now. This will pre-populate prefix cache for top talkers. Command (internal): ```./infra/tools/kv-sync --tenant cerulean --from eu-west-1 --to eu-west-2 --keys top_5000``` Expect ~90s to seed top keys.

infra-chen: I've requested additional warm hosts in eu-west-2 and pinned the dedicated capacity for Cerulean: +4 GPU nodes in warm state. ETA ~4m for provisioning. If provisioning fails we'll use burst-to-hostpool but that would mix tenancy.

cerulean-sre: We're following. We prefer DNS-based cutover. Can you also provide a short-lived IP list for our firewall? We have strict egress rules.

netops-rita: On it, generating allowlist for standby LB: `34.210.12.0/28, 52.19.45.0/28` (temporary). Sending to @cerulean-sre via secure channel.

alex_oncall: Plan summary: 1) seed KV + ensure model/version parity in eu-west-2, 2) provision + confirm warm hosts, 3) staged weighted DNS shift 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% (5m windows), 4) monitor error rate & latency, rollback if errors > 5% at any stage, 5) final DNS TTL back to normal and close. Anyone object?

observability-bot: [alert] cerulean:eu-west-1 error-rate=38% p99-latency=6.8s gpu-util=99% kv-evict-rate=high - triggered 6m ago

eng-ops-luis: I see warm nodes up in eu-west-2, KV seed completed (top_5000). Model binary verified checksum matches. GPUs show ready.

alex_oncall: @netops-rita can you prepare the Route53 change batch JSON? I'll hold the keys for manual apply.

netops-rita: change batch ready. snippet: ```{"Changes": [{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"cerulean.api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"CNAME","TTL":300,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"cerulean-eu-west-2-lb.redwood-inference.com"}]}}]}```

alex_oncall: executing first shift to 10%. I'm going to add a weighted entry rather than full swap: `cerulean.api -> 90% eu-west-1, 10% eu-west-2`. Applying now.

observability-bot: [metric-stream] after 10% shift: eu-west-1 error-rate -> 35%, eu-west-2 error-rate -> 12%, overall error-rate -> 31%

support-maya: Cerulean says some requests on the new host return 200 but with slower cold-starts for rare prefixes. They're OK with staged ramp.

alex_oncall: proceed to 30% in 5m. netops please apply next weighted edit.

netops-rita: applied 30/70. Monitoring.

observability-bot: after 30%: eu-west-1 error-rate 28%, eu-west-2 error-rate 8%, overall 24%

eng-ops-luis: p99 latency improving in eu-west-1 as load reduces. No new OOMs. KV eviction down by 60%.

cerulean-sre: we're seeing steady success. No client-side issues. Continuing to accept traffic to standby.

alex_oncall: moving to 60%. If metrics stay green we'll finalize 100% and decommission traffic to eu-west-1 for Cerulean.

netops-rita: applied 60/40 then 100/0 after the green light. Also pushing TTL down to 60s for final stabilization.

observability-bot: after 100% shift: eu-west-1 error-rate drops to 6% (background noise), eu-west-2 error-rate 2%, overall 3% - alert suppressed.

sre_jamie: post-cutover checklist: (a) mark eu-west-1 dedicated pool as drained for Cerulean client, (b) collect and snapshot logs for forensic, (c) schedule backfill of any missing KV keys, (d) prepare rollback plan to restore traffic to eu-west-1 if anomalies appear.

eng-ops-luis: draining now: `./infra/drain-tenant --tenant cerulean --region eu-west-1 --mode graceful` will stop new connectors but allow in-flight tokens to finish.

observability-bot: drain completed. No active requests on drained hosts.

alex_oncall: @cerulean-sre can you confirm client connectivity and that their firewall accepted the standby LB IPs?

cerulean-sre: confirmed. We had to add two rules but connections established and auth headers verified. All green from our side.

customer-success-evan: I updated Cerulean SOC and product leads. They're appreciative of the staged approach. They asked for an RCA and timeline for why autoscaler couldn't allocate earlier.

infra-chen: noted. Autoscaler hit soft quota due to concurrent provisioning across multiple customers. We have an action to improve priority preemption for enterprise reserved pools.

alex_oncall: I'm going to hand off to @sre_jamie for post-incident wrap and postmortem. Jamie, take over.

sre_jamie: taking handoff. I'll keep WATCH for 60m to ensure stability. Next steps: schedule a postmortem with Cerulean for root cause and action items, include quota change, autoscaler priority rule, and DNS failover runbook updates. Please add any logs to the incident folder (CER-2029-01).

netops-rita: I've restored normal TTL to 300s and removed temporary IP allowlists after confirmation from Cerulean.

alex_oncall: closing the active page. Thanks all for fast coordination. I'll tag this P1 and start the incident timeline.

cerulean-sre: thank you team — nice job on the staged cutover. We'll coordinate the postmortem schedule.

observability-bot: final snapshot: pre-cutover overall error-rate 38% -> post-cutover 3%, p99-latency down from 6.8s -> 0.9s. Incident CER-2029-01 resolved at 2290013399 UTC.

sre_jamie: Incident resolved. Follow-ups: (1) autoscaler quota/provisioning improvements, (2) improve warm cache priming speed, (3) update runbook for weighted DNS shifts + TTL guidance, (4) test tenant isolation in dedicated pools via chaos exercise. Assigning owners in the PM board. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
